title: Fuzz Testing
concept: Fuzz testing feeds random, valid, or near-valid input to the compiler to find crashes, hangs, and unexpected behaviors.
why: Humans write predictable tests. Fuzzers explore the unexpected — finding bugs in edge cases that no human tester would think to try.
syntax_ref:
# Fuzzing commands:
xiom fuzz --time 3600           # Fuzz for 1 hour
xiom fuzz --reproduce crash.xi  # Re-run a found crash
xiom fuzz --grammar             # Grammar-based fuzzing
xiom fuzz --coverage            # Coverage-guided fuzzing
tips: Fuzzers find bugs humans miss — every compiler release should be fuzzed
Grammar-based fuzzing produces VALID programs — catches compiler bugs, not parser bugs
Mutation fuzzing catches parser bugs — slightly invalid programs shouldn't crash the parser
Save ALL crashing inputs — they become regression tests to prevent recurrence
common_mistakes: Not fuzzing long enough — some bugs only appear after millions of iterations
Ignoring fuzzer findings — every crash is a real bug, fix it
Fuzzing without coverage feedback — random input without coverage guidance is inefficient
